t: This entry is the British Empire itself, rather than a single spot you can stand in front of. At its height it was the largest empire in history. By 1913 it held sway over 412 million people, about a quarter of the world's population. It began with English trading posts and overseas possessions in the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. The people linked to it here include missionaries such as John Stronach and Alexander Stronach, who worked in China with the London Missionary Society, and the physician John Dudgeon, who spent nearly forty years there.
